questions.question: What was Joseph Stalin's birth name?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Stalin was born Ioseb Besarionis dze Jughashvili.
Incorrect. Joseph Vissarionovich Stalin was his later name, not his birth name.
Incorrect. Iosif Vissarionovich Dzhugashvili was the Russified version of his birth name.
Incorrect. Koba was a nickname he adopted from a bandit protagonist, not his birth name.

questions.question: When did Joseph Stalin die?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Stalin ruled until his death in 1953 and gives the specific date of 5 March 1953.
Incorrect. 18 December 1878 is Stalin's birth date.
Incorrect. 1924 is the year Lenin died and Stalin assumed leadership.
Incorrect. 1945 is when the Red Army captured Berlin, ending World War II in Europe.

questions.question: Where was Stalin born?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Stalin was born into a poor Georgian family in Gori, Russian Empire.
Incorrect. Tiflis is where he attended seminary, not where he was born.
Incorrect. Baku is where he was located during the 1905 ethnic violence, not his birthplace.
Incorrect. Vienna is where he traveled in 1913 to research the national question, not his birthplace.

questions.question: Which political party did Stalin join as a youth?
options: Communist Party of the Soviet Union
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Stalin began his revolutionary career by joining the Marxist Russian Social Democratic Labour Party as a youth.
Incorrect. The Communist Party of the Soviet Union is the later name of the party he led, not the one he joined as a youth.
Incorrect. The Mensheviks were a faction within the RSDLP that Stalin opposed; he aligned with the Bolsheviks.
Incorrect. The Communist International was an organization through which Stalin's government promoted Marxism-Leninism abroad, not a party he joined as a youth.

questions.question: What newspaper did Stalin edit as a youth?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that as a youth in the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party, Stalin edited the party's newspaper, Pravda.
Incorrect. Proletariatis Brdzola was a Marxist newspaper he co-edited after escaping exile in 1904, not as a youth.
Incorrect. Zvezda was the Bolshevik weekly newspaper he later converted into Pravda, not the one he edited as a youth.
Incorrect. Das Kapital is Karl Marx's work that Stalin read, not a newspaper he edited.

questions.question: What title did Stalin hold from 1922 to 1952?
options: General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Stalin held the title of General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1922 to 1952.
Incorrect. Stalin was Premier from 1941 to 1953, not from 1922 to 1952.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Stalin holding the title of President of the Soviet Union.
Incorrect. The article mentions Stalin joined the Politburo but does not say he held the title of Chairman from 1922 to 1952.

questions.question: What replaced Lenin's New Economic Policy under Stalin?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Lenin's New Economic Policy was replaced with a centralized command economy.
Incorrect. The Five-Year Plan system was implemented under the command economy but is not described as the direct replacement for the New Economic Policy.
Incorrect. Collectivisation occurred under the Five-Year Plan system but is not described as the replacement for the New Economic Policy.
Incorrect. Socialism in One Country became a central tenet of party dogma but is not described as the replacement for the New Economic Policy.

questions.question: What event ended World War II in Europe according to the article?
options: The Red Army captured Berlin in 1945
Germany invaded the Soviet Union in 1941
The Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact with Nazi Germany
The Soviet Union annexed the Baltic states
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the Red Army captured Berlin in 1945, ending World War II in Europe.
Incorrect. Germany invading the Soviet Union in 1941 ended the non-aggression pact, not World War II.
Incorrect. The non-aggression pact was signed in 1939, before World War II ended.
Incorrect. The annexation of the Baltic states occurred after the war began, not as the event that ended it.

questions.question: Who succeeded Stalin after his death in 1953?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Stalin was eventually succeeded by Nikita Khrushchev.
Incorrect. Vladimir Lenin died in 1924, before Stalin.
Incorrect. Leon Trotsky is not mentioned in the article as Stalin's successor.
Incorrect. Georgy Malenkov is not mentioned in the article as Stalin's successor.

questions.question: What process did Khrushchev initiate after denouncing Stalin?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Khrushchev denounced Stalin and initiated a de-Stalinisation process throughout Soviet society.
Incorrect. Collectivisation was a policy under Stalin, not a process initiated by Khrushchev after denouncing him.
Incorrect. The Great Purge was instituted by Stalin, not by Khrushchev.
Incorrect. The New Economic Policy was Lenin's policy that Stalin replaced, not something Khrushchev initiated.
